text:
raj.k: FYI seeing repeated provisioning failures in us-west2 yesterday morning. GPU jobs hit node-level IO saturation and eviction. Root cause looks like cluster-wide NVMe GC/compaction storms after a rolling reboot window. digging in logs now.

jen: ugh. do we have a heatmap or timeline? is this correlated to a firmware push or kernel update?

raj.k: timeline: we rebooted a subset of the fleet for kernel security patches 03:10-03:45 UTC. ~10m after each host came up we saw a 10-20s sustained iops spike and then repeated background compactions for ~30-60m. affected nodes show high write ampl and SMART reallocated_k sectors tick.

mike: can you paste iostat/sar snippet? also which drive models? might be vendor GC kicking in on cold-warm transitions.

raj.k: pasted few snippets:
```
03:24:12 nodex-07 iostat: Device:r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.7 142.3 32 24560 170.3 1.23 1.1 1.3 0.61 98.5
```
and a correlated dmesg excerpt: 
```
[03:25:01] nvme0: background_reclaim: starting compaction window=120s flags=0x2
[03:25:02] nvme0: gc: moved 1.2G pages written=3.8G
[03:25:12] nvme0: gc: moved 4.9G pages written=12.2G
```

ana_s: looks like compactor is rewriting hot blocks. that can cause large transient write amplification. we saw similar on a canary region last quarter but that one was triggered by stale overprovision settings + aggressive vendor GC.

jen: any immediate mitigations to stop provisioning failures? we need GPUs for a priority training job in 2 hrs.

mike: short term: 1) throttle batch scheduler for affected AZs (reduce parallel allocations into nodes) 2) bump the ephemeral-cleaner/gc-delay on startup to avoid simultaneous GC work across all hosts 3) add an alert rule for sustained nvme write throughput > 150k kb/s for > 60s so oncall can pause incoming jobs.

raj.k: implemented throttling for the batch scheduler for us-west2-A,C (reduced concurrency by 60%) and bumped our local-agent startup delay from 30s to 6m for GC-trigger logic. observed drop in provisioning failures. infra-oncall-bot: automated alert added -> nvme_write_spike_uswest2.

infra-oncall-bot: Alert created: nvme_write_spike_uswest2 threshold=150000KB/s duration=60s channels=#oncall, #eng-infra

ana_s: good. longer term we need: vendor engagement to get GC tuning suggestions or firmware with more gradual background compaction, changes to overprovisioning and host startup staging, and maybe a canary rolling strategy so we never have >10% of nodes in warm-up concurrently.

mike: add a runbook step to detect nodes with SMART reallocated sectors > 0 and move them out of GPU pool for extra validation. also quantify cost impact: write_ampl x hours x nodes = egress and wear cost. can someone estimate?

raj.k: quick calc: ~40 nodes affected, avg extra writes ~8GB over 45m => ~320GB extra host writes. costs are low but wear acceleration is the worry. filing a vendor ticket with logs + heatmap. ticket #INF-4521.

jen: thanks. can you attach a small heatmap showing per-node start time vs iops? that helped before.

raj.k: attaching a link to grafana panel (private): https://grafana.internal/r/abcd1234/nvme-gc-heatmap (note: internal only). panel shows clear vertical bands matching our rolling reboots.

ana_s: for the vendor ticket include: firmware version, nvme vendor/model, config of overprovision (if any), host startup scripts that touch the device (e.g., fsck/trims), and the heatmap. ask for recommended background compaction schedule or an on-host throttle API.

mike: I'll schedule a canary plan: next maintenance window we'll do a staged reboot with 5% increments, wait 30m between groups, and monitor nvme_write_spike alert. if no spike, widen. otherwise vendor patch.

raj.k: note — we also saw that nodes with our ephemeral-cleaner disabled did not hit the same amplitude, so the cleaner is likely triggering extra GC by proactively trimming/rewriting. we'll add a toggle to skip full cleaner runs for 24h post-boot.

jen: perfect. please paste the vendor ticket link once created and mark priority-high.

raj.k: done. INF-4521 created and linked in ticketing system: https://tickets.internal/INF-4521. assigning to ana_s for vendor follow-up. :thumbsup:

ana_s: ack, I'll ping vendor tomorrow morning. also proposing we add an integration test that simulates warm-up compaction on a spare node to validate mitigations before any mass rollout.

mike: +1. add that to infra backlog and assign to eng-infra/testing.

jen: thanks all. follow-ups: canary plan doc, vendor ticket, runbook updates, and the new alert. looks like the immediate fix held. closing this thread after we confirm next maintenance window results. :white_check_mark:
